title: Data and Machine Learning for Biotech
subtitle: Everything an entry-level data or assay role in biotech and medtech asks for: Python, lab data, statistics, QC, and machine learning on assay and instrument data.
preface: This book is written for one purpose: to teach you what an entry-level data, assay or R&D role at a biotech or medical device company expects, without sending you to another book. It starts from zero. If you can run a Python script after the first chapter, you have what you need for the second.

Each chapter ends with a quiz and worked problems drawn from real lab situations: plate reader files, calibration curves, replicate statistics, control charts. The chapters are written so you can describe the work in an interview and do it on the job.

Planned later parts, to be added: statistics for lab decisions (confidence intervals, t-tests, ANOVA, method comparison), machine learning on assay and instrument data with scikit-learn, introductory bioinformatics (sequences, alignments, single-cell workflows), and data work in regulated settings (validation, traceability, audit trails).

parts.title: Foundations of Lab Data
parts.blurb: Python for tables and plots, then the calculations behind every assay result.
